strategy.summary: Slévárna Vrbenský is a small, financially sound, family-owned Czech foundry. It is our cheaper second source for volute casing part:310050: a 25% quota, against sup:70180 at 75% and a much higher price. It has cut its price steadily since 2023 and has settled below its own ask in every renewal. It has just doubled its stainless moulding capacity (news:20260420-09), so it wants volume. It values cash: it asked for 10-day payment against a cash discount (doc:20260210-70170-M1). It also values us as a reference customer (doc:20260512-70170-M2). Its weak spot is recent performance: delivery fell below the contract target and quality slipped, with two complaints and the scorecard now class C red (sc:70170@2026Q3). This may be ramp-up strain. Its strongest cost argument is the 1.4404 alloy surcharge over 12 months. There is no should-cost, so margin is unknown. Our real economic lever is shifting quota toward it, not squeezing its unit price, since the alternative source is far dearer. Pair any volume shift with quality and delivery commitments.

It has always settled below its ask, so it will move a little in exchange for volume, cash and length. Big unit cuts are unlikely and unjustified without should-cost.

strategy.writer_notes: The core play is more volume or quota share, a binding commitment and faster payment in exchange for a stable or lower price plus a quality and on-time commitment. Our gain comes from moving share away from the dearer source, so do not squeeze this supplier's margin. Acknowledge its new line and its reference status. Expect alloy and labour claims, and counter only with the recent alloy fall and the power decline. Check whether any price-change notice met the contractual notice period. Evidence on decision makers, hedging and margin is thin.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for part:310050, so margin over full cost cannot be measured; evidence on price room is indirect (price history, rival prices, driver indices). Treat any margin claim as thin.

Vrbenský is already the cheap source: EUR 559.61 since 2026-01 versus sup:70180 at EUR 654.52 (+17%), and in rfq:6000000105 it quoted 598.10 vs 676.60 yet lost the award (quota 25% vs 75%). Its price has fallen -7.6% since 2023 (605.33 -> 569.40 -> 569.40 -> 559.61). Little evidence of fat; pushing hard on price risks margin, but it also means it has reason to want more share.

Weighted driver movement over 12 months is roughly neutral-to-slightly-up: labour LCI-C +2.7% x0.26 = +0.69%, alloy AS-14404 +5.9% x0.24 = +1.42%, power PPI-D351 -3.7% x0.06 = -0.22%; net about +1.9% on price. Remaining ~44% of cost weight has no driver. A small increase claim (~1.5-2%) would be index-supported if raised.

Counter-points on cost: alloy surcharge has fallen -5.5% since its 2026-06 high (recent trend down) and sits -13% below its 36-month peak; power -15% below 2024-11 peak and -43.5% below 2022. Since the 2026 price was set (late 2025), alloy is roughly +6.6% from 2025-12 low, so the alloy argument is the supplier's strongest.

Negotiation history: three renewals settled on average 2.3 pp below its ask; last time asked +0.6%, settled -1.7%. Price fixed per calendar year; changes need 90 days' notice before year-end (i.e. by early October for 2027).

Non-price levers with value: it asked for 10-day payment with cash discount (values cash); new moulding line doubled stainless capacity (wants volume); forecast 1593 vs 1406 pcs. Quality slipped (5682 ppm, 2 complaints on this part) and OTD 91.7% vs 95% target.

findings.text: Small family-owned Czech foundry (150 staff, EUR 8.27 M turnover, founded 1997). Decisions likely sit with the owner family, so the approval ladder is short. Finances are sound and stable: equity ratio 36.4%, credit index 239 unchanged in 12 months. There is no sign of financial stress, and it can afford to walk away. Evidence on individual decision makers is absent.

It values cash. In Feb 2026 it asked us to pay invoices within 10 days and offered a cash discount. We currently pay at 45 days net, and 92.3% of invoices are paid late (avg 5.2 days, max 13). Faster or on-time payment is a cheap trade currency for us. Our late payment is also a sensitivity it can raise against us.

It has new capacity to fill. A new automatic moulding line commissioned in April 2026 doubles its stainless casting capacity. It holds only a 25% quota on part 310050, and our forecast volume is rising (1593 vs 1406). Extra volume or quota share is what it most needs.

It seeks recognition and the relationship. It called Hollerau an important reference customer at the supplier day and invited us to its fair booth. Respectful, relationship-framed messages should land well. Our spend is only 2.4% of its turnover, so its interest is reputational more than financial.

Its performance has slipped. Over the last 12 months, on-time delivery was 91.7% against a 95% target (100% a year earlier). Quality was 5682 ppm from 2 complaints, against a peer median of 457 ppm, and one 8D is still unclosed. Possibly this is ramp-up strain from the new line. This weakens its position.

Negotiation style: it concedes readily. Over 3 renewals it settled on average 2.3 pp below its ask, and in the last one it asked +0.6% and settled at -1.7%. It is also far cheaper than the rival (EUR 654.52 vs 559.61), so it knows it is competitive and owns the tooling.

findings.text: Framework agreement covers only part:310050 (Volute casing HI 80-250), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). Exit remains a credible, still-open option.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Changes need written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2 Oct for a 2027 change. A supplier increase request arriving late in the year cannot take effect on 1 Jan 2027. This needs checking against when any request was received.

Payment is 45 days net, shorter than our 60-day standard, which already benefits the supplier. Delivery is FCA with a 56-day lead time; our planned lead time is 49. The supplier asked in Feb 2026 for 10-day payment against a cash discount, so it values cash. We pay on average 5.2 days late, which it can raise against us.

The quality clause sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. Rolling on-time delivery is 91.7%, below target, and ppm is 5682 from 2 complaints, with one 8D still open. Both are a contractual breach-of-target argument, although the EUR 150 fee is a weak deterrent.

In the last three renewals the supplier asked for an average of -0.2% and settled at -2.5%. It settled below its ask every time: -2.5% to -5.9%, +1.2% to 0, and +0.6% to -1.7%. Its price fell from 605.33 to 559.61 (-7.6%) since 2023. This history is short (3 events) but consistent.

The supplier holds a 25% quota on part:310050 next to sup:70180 at 75%, whose tooling Hollerau owns. This supplier owns its own tooling, so the 75% source is ready but moving all volume costs nothing tooling-wise only at the rival. However, the rival is ~17% dearer (654.52 vs 559.61) and quoted 676.60 in the 2025 RFQ, so shifting volume away is costly for us.

Mutual dependency is low. Our spend is ~EUR 199k, about 2.4% of its EUR 8.27M turnover. Spend is growing (152k to 199k), and need is up to 1593 pcs from 1406. It has doubled its stainless capacity and calls us a reference customer, so it wants more volume. Our lever is quota shift up from 25%, not threat of exit.

findings.text: Performance has deteriorated from a perfect record to class C red. Rolling OTD was 100% through 2025Q3 and has fallen to 91.7% against the requested date. That is below the 95% target, although it is still 95.8% against its own confirmed date. The score dropped from 100 to 67.4 over the last four quarters.

Quality has slipped from 0 ppm to 5682 ppm, against a peer median of 457. The base is only 2 single-piece complaints on part:310050 (burr; porosity), so the ppm figure is jumpy and the evidence is thin. The porosity QN of 2026-08-26 has no closed 8D yet but is not overdue. EUR 150 has been recharged, as per the flat fee.

Lateness is moderate. Over the last 12 months 2 of 24 receipts were late, averaging 8.5 days and at most 10. The requested-vs-confirmed data has a known issue, so we should argue from the scorecard figures. Recent POs were confirmed on the requested dates.

The alternative source sup:70180 delivers about 3x the volume at 0 ppm but costs 654.52 against 559.61, about 17% more. On price, Vrbenský is clearly the cheaper source; its weakness is quality and delivery.

The volume outlook is positive. The forecast is 1593 pcs for the next 12 months against 1406 ordered, and it has been shared with suppliers. Vrbenský's share is about 25% (344 pcs in the last 12 months). Its newly doubled capacity makes a quota shift towards it attractive to the supplier, which we can trade for price and quality commitments.
Price history favours the supplier's narrative. It has cut from 605.33 to 559.61 (-7.6%) since 2023.

arguments.text: We are already the cheapest source by a wide margin: EUR 559.61 vs EUR 654.52 at Feinguss Allgäu-Reiter (about 14.5 % below). In the July 2025 benchmark we quoted 598.10 against their 676.60 and still lost the award. Every further cut comes out of a margin we have already given up three times.

Our price has fallen 7.6 % since 2023 (605.33 to 559.61). Over the same period our cost drivers rose. Labour, about 26 % of our cost, is up 2.7 % in 12 months. The 1.4404 alloy surcharge, about 24 %, is up 5.9 % to EUR 3,008/t. Steel is up 7.3 % since January, and iron castings producer prices are up 1.8 %. The weighted drivers net to roughly +2 %, so a hold is already a real concession.

We are a healthy, stable second source for an A-part. We have 36 % equity, an unchanged credit index, and ISO 9001/14001/50001. Our new automatic moulding line doubles our stainless capacity. That gives Hollerau security of supply that a single source at 75 % cannot.

From 2024 to 2025 our delivery record was 100 % on time with zero ppm for several scorecard periods. The recent dip is ramp-up strain from the new line, and confirmed-date OTD is still 95.8 %, above the 95 % contract target. Both 8D reports have been worked on, none is overdue, and the burr complaint is closed.
Hollerau pays late: 92 % of invoices are paid after the due date, on average 5.5 days and up to 13 days. That is financing cost we carry on top of the 45-day terms.

weak_points: Scorecard has dropped to class C red (67.4); OTD against the requested date is 91.7 %, below the 95 % target.
Porosity complaint qn:20005004 still has an open 8D, and ppm last 12m is 5682 while Feinguss is at 0 ppm.
Electricity is down 3.7 % y/y and 43 % from the 2022 peak; we are an energy-intensive foundry.
The alloy surcharge is 13 % below its 36-month peak and fell 5.5 % within the year; 1.4404 is a proxy, our casting grade is 1.4408.
We openly need volume for the new line and cash (the 10-day payment request), which signals that we are eager.
We have settled below our ask in every renewal, which shows we fold.
The tooling is ours, which makes it harder for them to leave, but we only hold 25 % quota.
Copper +48 % and electronics +41 % do not apply to us, so citing them would cost us credibility.
wants: A quota shift from 25 % toward 40-50 % of the roughly 1,600 pcs/yr forecast, with a binding annual volume.
Payment within 10 days against a cash discount of about 2 %, or at least on-time payment at 30-45 days.
A contract extension to 24-36 months at a fixed price.
Optionally, an alloy surcharge clause on 1.4408 with a symmetric band.
Permission to use Hollerau as a public reference.
red_lines: No price below about EUR 545 without a binding volume increase.
No further cut alongside a quota held at 25 %.
No ppm penalty or chargeback per complaint above the EUR 150 flat fee without a volume commitment.
No retroactive price change; the 90-day calendar-year rule applies.
No lead time shorter than 49 days during the ramp-up.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the partnership and acknowledge the recent delivery and quality dip openly. Explain it as ramp-up of the new line and present the corrective actions: the porosity 8D close date and moulding process controls. Point out that we are 14 % below the alternative source and have cut prices three times while alloy and labour rose. Propose holding EUR 559.61 for 2027 (an opening ask of +1.5 %, settling at 0). In exchange for a quota move to 40 %+ with binding volume, 10-day payment with a 2 % discount, and a 24-month extension, offer about -1 to -2 % plus OTD and ppm commitments.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that your price is competitive, and we value that; it is one reason we see you as a supplier to grow with. But the comparison with the other source does not set your price, your own cost and the volume we give you do. What we pay you today is our starting point, and we do not ask you to give up margin for nothing. We would rather talk about a larger and more secure share for you on this casing, which fills your new line, against a stable price.

We accept that labour and the alloy surcharge have risen over the year, and we take your cost pressure seriously. In proportion, though, the alloy surcharge has already fallen clearly from its recent high, and power, a real cost for a foundry, is lower than a year ago. Weighted by their share, these drivers net to far less than you suggest. Steel and iron casting price indices do not describe a stainless casting and should not be counted on top. Your earlier reductions were agreed against rising volumes, which continue.

We agree: you are financially sound, well certified, and your new moulding line is good news for us as well as for you. That is why we can offer you more work on this part. Security of supply, however, shows in the delivery and quality record, and that has weakened since the new line started. If more share is to move to you, we need to see the performance return to the level you showed before.

Your earlier record was excellent, and we recognise that the dip may come from the ramp-up. The contract target, however, is measured against our requested date, where you are now below target and your scorecard has dropped markedly. We do not want to overstate a few single-piece complaints, but before we shift volume we would like a firm on-time and quality commitment, which we see as something to fix together.

That is a fair point and we will not argue it: our payments have often been a few days late, and we will commit to paying on time. We also remember your request for faster payment against a cash discount. We are open to discussing shorter payment terms as part of the overall package, priced fairly against that discount.

press: We would welcome a concrete plan showing when on-time delivery against our requested dates will be back at the contract target.
Since power costs have eased over the past year, we would expect this to be reflected alongside the labour and alloy figures you mention.
The alloy surcharge has fallen noticeably from its recent high, so we would ask you to weigh that movement as well.
Our shared forecast shows rising volume, and we would like to discuss how much of it your new line could take reliably.
We would be glad to hear what cash discount you would offer if we moved to faster payment, as you suggested earlier.
Given that our past renewals have always found a balanced settlement, we are confident we can do so again in exchange for more volume and a longer commitment.
